title: zero-downtime KMS key promotion and HSM rolling-upgrade hooks (Helm + Terraform)
author: Ethan Huang
release_notes:
- Add zero-downtime KMS key promotion orchestration for HSM-backed clusters
- Helm hooks to coordinate TLS cert rotation and sealed-secrets reconciliation during upgrades
- Terraform module updates: kms_binding resource and promotion state bucket
- Rollback-safe upgrade path with staged promotion and automatic demote on failure
description:
Motivation: Private deployments using HSM-backed KMS saw transient outages during KMS key rotations and HSM rolling upgrades. Customers running on-prem environments require predictable promotions of a newly generated primary key without a service-wide lock or manual intervention. This PR introduces orchestration and tooling to perform zero-downtime KMS key promotions tied to the installer (Helm) lifecycle and Terraform orchestration.

Summary of changes: implemented a coordinated promotion workflow that: 1) introduces a promotion state object stored in a customer-controlled S3/GCS bucket and reconciled by the installer; 2) exposes a Helm pre-upgrade hook to stage TLS certificate replacement and sealed-secrets reconciliation; 3) adds a Terraform module (kms_promotion) to create the state bucket, IAM bindings, and an optional IAM service account used during promotion; 4) provides a small state machine sidecar (k8s job template) to perform promotion steps against an HSM-backed KMS via existing KMS operator CRDs; 5) adds canary mode flags so operators can promote a single region/replica first and automatically rollback if health checks fail.

Design notes: the promotion state is intentionally external (object in bucket + locking) to allow cross-cluster coordination and safe retries. The Helm hooks perform three ordered phases (stage -> promote -> finalize) and are idempotent. During promote, the sidecar populates the HSM key metadata and flips the 'primary' marker in KMS operator CRD; traffic is gradually shifted using a routing label toggled by the installer. Rollback paths demote the key and reconcile secrets to the previous primary.

Files changed (high level): sources/helm/redwood-private/values.yaml (new canary flags), charts/redwood-private/templates/hooks/promote-hook-job.yaml (hook job template), charts/redwood-private/templates/hooks/finalize-cleanup-job.yaml, terraform/modules/kms_promotion/main.tf, terraform/modules/kms_promotion/outputs.tf, terraform/modules/kms_promotion/variables.tf, docs/installer/kms-promotion.md (usage + troubleshooting), scripts/ci/compose-promotion-test.sh, pkg/kms/sidecar/handler.go (promotion state machine), pkg/kms/README.md, tests/integration/promotion-smoke.test (new), tests/upgrade/rollback-e2e.yaml (example).

Testing and verification: added unit tests for the state machine logic and Helm hook templates. Integration smoke test runs in our CI using an HSM simulator image to validate key lifecycle operations and sealed-secrets reconciliation. Manual QA performed in a lab VPC: executed canary promote (single-node) then staged full promotion across three-node cluster; we simulated a failing finalize stage to verify automatic demote and rollback of TLS + sealed-secrets. CI matrix: linux/amd64 + HSM-sim container; full e2e in gated pipeline passed.

Rollback and safety: promote job is guarded by locks in the bucket and will abort if a concurrent promotion is detected. Health checks (readiness on routing-proxy and KMS operator status) are evaluated after promote stage; failure triggers demote. No data encryption keys are re-encrypted during the promotion—only the primary marker moves; consumer services read both primary and previous-primary for overlap window to allow zero-downtime.

Operational playbook (short): 1) Run terraform apply for kms_promotion to provision bucket + SA. 2) Set values.canary.promotion = true in values.yaml and helm upgrade --install. 3) Monitor promotetask CRD and routing-proxy metrics. 4) If finalize fails, operator may rely on automatic demote or run helm uninstall --hook for manual demote. See docs/installer/kms-promotion.md for full steps.

Related: builds on prior sealing automation and HSM enrollment work (see ENG-1702). This PR intentionally avoids changing KMS operator internals; instead it uses operator CRDs and a lightweight job/sidecar to orchestrate.

Checklist: - [x] Terraform module created and documented - [x] Helm hooks added and tested - [x] Sidecar state machine implemented with unit tests - [x] Integration smoke tests added to CI - [x] Docs and troubleshooting guide written - [x] Reviewed and approved by security and SRE

review_discussion:
Anika Shah: Can you clarify how the bucket lock handles a partial write?
Ethan Huang: The sidecar writes a txn JSON and then an atomic rename; we added verification to detect partial writes and to abort if checksum mismatches.
Luca Moretti: Does this require extra IAM scopes?
Ethan Huang: TF creates a minimal SA with write/list/objectLock permissions limited to the promotion bucket; documented in variables.tf.
Priya Nair: Please add an operator-visible event when demote happens.
Ethan Huang: Added an event emitter in the sidecar and bumped tests to assert event presence.
Anika Shah: Approved after CI fixed flaky e2e (re-ran).
